sources.name: YouGov: Americans' favorite condiments (love %, ownership %; 22 condiments surveyed, only top 10 'love' + 11 'own' published)
sources.method: poll of 1,104 US adult citizens, Jan 30-Feb 1 2026

sources.name: Circana/Amazon Fresh condiment category sales (Food Institute)
sources.method: sales data, 52 wks ending Jul 2 2023 (mayo, ketchup, pickles, mustard only)

sources.name: DoorDash grocery burger-condiment orders (Fox 5 Atlanta)
sources.method: delivery order data May 2022-Mar 2023, top 5 only

changes_vs_current: Data only supports positions 1-10 (ketchup, mayo, mustard, ranch, hot sauce, salsa, BBQ, relish, pickles, soy sauce); mayo/mustard moved up, ranch/hot sauce/salsa down. Positions 11-24 are carried over from the current list in current order (avg 10.5 = 'no data' value, not a measured rank); Worcestershire dropped only to make room for Pickles. I excluded peanut butter, honey, chocolate sauce, maple syrup and jam from the YouGov list as spreads/toppings (they were #1,2,5,7,8 in YouGov's 'love' ranking) - add back if you want them as condiments.
confidence: low - no source ranks more than 10 condiments; four short lists of mixed method (poll love %, sales, delivery orders, reader poll). Top ~5 (ketchup/mayo/mustard/ranch/hot sauce) is consistent across sources. Positions 11-24 are NOT data-backed. Ranker condiments page was blocked (HTTP 401), and Instacart/Harris 2021 only gave 'most hated' lists.
